# 1.2 Prefix sums and difference arrays (1D, 2D)

Phase 1 (Array techniques), target rating 1000–1400. Bank status: not started.

## Patterns

### Static range sums (`range-sum`)

Answer many sum queries over ranges of a fixed array in O(1) each after O(n) preparation.

**Works because:** The array does not change, and the operation can be undone (sums: subtract the prefix before l).

### Pairs of prefix values (`prefix-count-lookup`)

Count subarrays whose sum equals k, or is divisible by k, by counting earlier prefix values in a map.

**Works because:** The condition on a subarray [l, r] is a condition on the pair of prefix values P[r] and P[l−1] alone.

### Many range updates, then read (`difference-array`)

Apply many "add v to every element in [l, r]" updates, then read the final array once.

**Works because:** All updates come before all reads (offline), so each update is two point changes in the difference array.

### Rectangle sums in a grid (`prefix-2d`)

Sum over any sub-rectangle of a fixed grid via the four-corner formula; also 2D range updates read once.

**Works because:** The grid is static, and the rectangle sum equals a signed combination of four prefix rectangles.

### Prefix and suffix extremes (`prefix-extremes`)

Precompute prefix and suffix maxima or minima to answer "best value excluding position i" or "best split point".

**Works because:** The extreme of a prefix (or suffix) can only grow (or shrink) as it extends, so one pass computes all of them.
